environmental.operating-temp: to 70 C - 325 A per panel at 45 C, de-rated to 200 A at 70 C; no lower limit is stated

management.alarm-contacts: Form C relay per side, 2 A at 30 VDC and 0.6 A at 60 VDC, on wire-wrap terminals

physical.overall-mm: 431.8 x 44 x 478 without tie bar, 559 deep with the tie bar it ships with (17 x 1.75 x 18.8 in)
physical.weight-configured-scope: populated, 19.6 lb in the datasheet; unpopulated is 14.6 lb

power.input-dc: dual feed; maximum input load 325 A at 45 C per panel, de-rated to 200 A at 70 C; input wire 2/0 AWG to 350 MCM; output wire #14 to #6 AWG in P40 connectors
power.output-breaker-max: 60 A single-pole; the UL rating holds to 48 A continuous per output
power.power-max-scope: the alarm card alone at 48 V (30 mA); 0.48 W at 24 V and 0.22 W at 12 V. THE MONITORING CARD ALSO DRAWS FROM THE A AND B FEEDS, and no document held states how much (gap monitoring-card-draw), so this figure is a floor for the panel, not its total. Separately the guide gives a nominal power LOSS of less than 45 W per side at 325 A and 48 V, which is heat in the conductors and not a draw.

configs.description: The panel as it ships: no breakers, a blanking cover over every position, and no output plugs. Breakers and connector kits are sold separately.
configs.name: base

configs.description: All sixteen positions fitted with breakers behind their touch guards, as every product photograph shows the panel, with an invented spread of ratings. An illustration, not an orderable bundle.
configs.name: populated

configs.description: Side A on breakers and side B on TPA fuses in their holders, to show the two things a position takes. An illustration; the vendor sells the holder and the fuses for this panel and publishes no standard fill.
configs.name: with-fuses

gaps.note: the TPA fuse holder, part 307492, is seated from three-quarter views only: its face is placed by eye and its size is borrowed from the breaker whose position it fits.

the power drawn by the nrgSMART card is stated nowhere in the datasheet, the installation guide, the controller datasheet or the two controller configuration guides; searched for mA, watt, consumption and current draw. `power-max-w` is the alarm card alone.

gaps.note: the two five-way nrgNET connectors are drawn at a 3.81 pitch, read off five ways in about 20 on Fig. 3-7; no document states the header or its pitch.

`physical-context` on 16 bays (front 16) - unlocks ENTITY-MIB / Redfish correlation and monitoring overlays

breaker-ratings.note: ONE MODULE CARRIES ELEVEN RATINGS AS A FIELD. The datasheet sells breakers from 2 A to 60 A as eleven part numbers that differ in nothing but the figure printed on the handle, so they are one part with a `rating` field, set per position in a configuration. Each breaker ships with a touch guard seated on it, a separate part that a configuration can take off. The populated example is an invented load to show the field working; the vendor publishes no standard fill.

chassis.note: 431.8 wide and 43.9 high as the 300CB08. THE DEPTH MODELLED IS THE CHASSIS, 330.8, the figure the plain panel bottom view dimensions. The datasheet gives this version as 478 deep without its tie bar: the extra 147 is the input busbars standing behind the chassis rear, and they are drawn as that, on the input parts. With the tie bar it is 559.

ears.note: NOT DRAWN. The panel ships with separate 19 inch and 23 inch mounting brackets (PMTG19, PMTG23) that bolt to the sides; Fig. 3-1 dimensions them at 482.6 and 584.2 over the body.

envelope-faces.note: Top, bottom, left and right are sized from the chassis. The bottom vent fields and its two ground bolts are placed from Fig. 3-12 at 1.336 px/mm, a coarse reading. The top is given the same two side fields the photographs show running the depth of the lid; their extent is estimated. The sides are placed from the side view, Fig. 3-4, at 1.717 px/mm: four bracket holes 29.1 apart starting 11.1 from the front, and a two-bolt ground landing 268.8 from the front. THE GROUND BOLTS ARE DRAWN ON THE STATED 5/8 INCH CENTRES, 15.9 apart, not the 18.3 the drawing measures, because the callout states the figure and the drawing is coarse. Each side carries one landing and the bottom a third; the guide says only one ground connection is required.

front.note: Breaker cells, thumbscrews, lamp holes, switch slots and the designation card slot are measured on Fig. 3-1. Sixteen cells 17.8 x 39.1 on a 19.81 pitch (39 px), the first at 14.2 and the ninth at 261.1, which mirror about the centre to a tenth. What is printed on the front comes from the front photograph in the same guide (Fig. 1-1) and its positions are fractions of the centre panel read off that photograph, which is taken from slightly above: the wording is as printed, the positions are approximate. The DC, alarm and electrostatic symbols are drawn as plain strokes in the places the photograph shows them; their exact artwork is not resolved at that size. The front prints in dark ink on the pale panel. THE MODEL LEGEND IS A JUDGEMENT: the photograph of a sensor panel in the guide (Fig. 1-3) shows the plain panel layout with a model name beginning nrg300CB08 at the top right, cut off by the frame. nrg300CB08-SENS is printed here, WITHOUT the -C suffix, as amphenol-ns/300cb08-c keeps the plain 300CB08 legend; no photograph of this version shows whether its face adds the suffix. Fig. 3-3, the sensor front view, draws a box at that place and a small square between the switch slots that no document names; they are taken to be the model and voltage legends.

front-cover.note: THE FRONT FACE IS A REMOVABLE COVER. The guide has a procedure for it (section 2.2.7): two thumbscrews release a bar that spans the front, with sixteen openings the breaker guards show through and the lamps, switch slots and card slot in its centre. It is drawn as the panel, not as a part, because the panel is never seen without it in service and the breakers, not the cover, are what a position holds. The slot under the lamps is the designation card holder the datasheet lists.

ground-stud-size.note: The installation guide is one document for every version of the panel and its grounding specification is not limited to a version, as its input rows are: three sets of 1/4-20 threaded holes on 5/8 inch centres, bolted with washers to 50 in-lb, for a dual-hole compression lug on #6 to #1 AWG wire. Its description says the ground terminals take either a dual-hole or a single-hole lug and that only one ground connection is required. That is the `stud-size` of all six ground placements, two on each side and two on the bottom.

lamps.note: Five lamps on a 12.7 pitch: A PWR, A ALM, nrg, B ALM, B PWR (Fig. 2-11 names them, Fig. 3-3 draws the five holes). PWR is green with its feed present and ALM red on an alarm, as on the plain panel. The nrg lamp is the monitoring card: the guide gives off, red, green and flashing red for the older nrg300CB08 in terms of nrgNET power, and the controller guide says the Identify button blinks it. Whether the sensor version keeps the older meanings is not stated; red, green and a blink are recorded and no more.

lifecycle.note: searched 2026-10-05 for an end-of-life, end-of-sale or discontinuation notice for the 300CB08 and found none; the vendor product page lists it as current. The installation guide marks a different part, the original nrg300CB08, as EOL and replaced by the -SENS and -CTRL versions.

method.note: THE MONITORED SENS PANEL WITH THE CONNECTORIZED -C REAR. The front, top, bottom and sides are amphenol-ns/nrg300cb08-sens and take its readings; the rear outputs, inputs, depth and weight are amphenol-ns/300cb08-c, whose datasheet rows this version shares, and the rear centre block is the monitored one, read off Fig. 3-9 of the installation guide.

monitoring.note: nrgSMART measures feed and per-circuit current, voltage and two probe temperatures. The controller and sensor electronics are powered from the A and B feeds, not from nrgNET (the nrgSMART integrated controller system configuration guide 151881). NO DOCUMENT HELD STATES WHAT THEY DRAW: the only power figure is the alarm card, 1.44 W at 48 V, which is what `power-max-w` carries here as it does on the plain panel. That figure is therefore low for this device by the draw of its monitoring card.

ratings.note: The datasheet gives the maximum input load as 325A @ 45 C per panel. The installation guide prints the same row with its de-rating: 325A @45 C per panel (De-rated to 200A @70 C). That is the only temperature either document states for the panel, so it is what `operating-temp` carries: a ceiling with its two rating points, and no lower limit.

rear.note: Fig. 3-8, the embedded 1399 x 199 image on page 40, at 2.849 px/mm, scaled on the body between its two edges (85 to 1315 px) taken as 431.8, which then reads 43.9 high. Sixteen P40 receptacles on a 13.41 pitch, as on the -SC. Each input is two horizontal busbar landings seen end-on, and the drawing prints what the stud versions do not: a large B at the left end and A at the right, and BATTERY and RETURN beside each assembly, BATTERY on the OUTER side of both. SIDE A IS THE MIRROR OF SIDE B: the narrow landing, 6.0 against 7.7, is the outer one on each (26.3 and 399.8 from the left), so the side A feed is the same part turned 180 degrees and its `landing-1` is BATTERY on both sides. THE CENTRE BLOCK IS THE MONITORED ONE: Fig. 3-9, the embedded 1399 x 199 image 3 on page 40, is Fig. 3-8 with two five-way nrgNET connectors and two probe jacks under the alarm headers, as Fig. 3-7 draws them for the stud-and-screw version; amphenol-ns/nrg-rear-block@1 is placed where the passive panel has its alarm card.

rear-cover.note: NOT DRAWN. A clear polycarbonate cover closes the whole rear over the input and output terminals (datasheet, Primary Features; guide Fig. 2-20). It is transparent and everything behind it is what the rear view shows.

tie-bar.note: NOT DRAWN. The panel ships with a rear tie bar for dressing the output cables (guide Fig. 2-2 and 2-25), and takes an optional four-post bracket kit, 307622. Cable management is not drawn; the datasheet depth with the bar fitted is recorded.
